newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates fall on fresh liquidity.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates fall on fresh liquidity.

text.p: Interbank rates dipped across the board following a sharp drop in Wednesday's overnight rate due to fresh liquidity in the system, dealers said on Thursday.
They said one-week money dipped to 6.60/70 percent against 7.45/50, two-week to 6.80/90 against 7.45/50 and one-month to 7.10/15 against 7.25/30.
Dealers said the fall in rates was in reaction to fall in the overnight rate to 6.0 percent from 8.3 on Wednesday.
"It is mainly large local and foreign banks which seem to be long," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said these banks suddenly became flush on Wednesday afternoon, which has pulled down interest rates.
Many dealers with small banks said they were not sure where the liquidity came from.
"It has to be either overseas funds or some Bank Negara maturities of funds directly raised from select banks," said a dealer with another Malaysian bank.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the domestic market to control liquidity or set interest rates. It sometimes approaches select banks directly to raise deposits.
Some dealers said banks could be preparing for the maturity of another 800 million ringgit in long-term government bonds on October 15.
